key_rules_and_shortcuts: Line Symmetry: Fold test causes two halves to overlap perfectly.
Regular n-gon has n lines of symmetry and smallest rotational angle 360°/n.
Ashoka Chakra (24 spokes) has 24 lines of symmetry and smallest rotational angle 15°.
unit_conversions_and_definitions: Order of Rotational Symmetry: Number of matching positions during a full 360° rotation

section_2_common_pitfalls_and_error_anal.frequent_exam_mistake: Assuming non-square rectangle diagonals are lines of symmetry.
section_2_common_pitfalls_and_error_anal.why_it_happens: Diagonals divide a rectangle into congruent triangles, so students assume they are lines of fold symmetry.
section_2_common_pitfalls_and_error_anal.correct_exam_approach: Folding a rectangle along a diagonal causes corners to overhang, not overlap. Rectangles have only 2 lines of symmetry (midsegments).

level_1_objective_and_recall_1_mark.question: What is the smallest angle of rotational symmetry for a regular pentagon?

level_2_direct_computational_2_marks.question: State the number of lines of symmetry and smallest rotational angle for a square.

level_3_multi_step_word_problems_3_to_5_.problem_statement: An architect designs a ceiling fan with 6 identical blades arranged symmetrically around a central motor.
level_3_multi_step_word_problems_3_to_5_.to_find: (a) Order of rotational symmetry. (b) All angles of rotation < 360°.

level_4_hots_and_competency_case_studies.case_scenario_text: Case Study: Testing Rotational Angle Validity. A student claims a figure has rotational symmetry with smallest angle 17°.

sub_questions.question: Determine whether the student's claim is mathematically possible.
sub_questions.detailed_solution: 360° / 17° = 21.176... Since 360° is not an exact integer multiple of 17°, it is IMPOSSIBLE for a figure to have 17° as its smallest angle of rotational symmetry.
